Headline exact: 'THE MACHINE KEEPS GOING'
Subtitle exact: 'ENDLESS MUSEUM · FORCE AND UNINTENDED COMEDY'
The one device throughout is an exposed spring-driven helper on a low pale wheeled trolley. Its simple metal hinged arm ends in a shallow spoon cradle for the black sphere; a spiral spring and a soft fabric sleeve wrapped on the arm are visible. This is an absurd but believable tool for moving a ball, not a humanoid robot. Keep same design across all panels.
PANEL 1: student stands at left and gently winds the helper's spring, black sphere sitting in spoon on trolley. The intended destination is an empty white plinth one meter to the right. Wide setup, readable relationship. Caption: 'I asked it to move the point.'
PANEL 2: the spring arm swings to the right toward the empty plinth. The trolley recoils left on its wheels and the spoon undershoots; black ball rolls off spoon onto the floor. Student leans after it with open hands, deadpan rather than hurt. Small restrained drawn motion streaks show swinging and rolling, no extra balls. Caption: 'The trolley moves as well.'
PANEL 3: same trolley's sleeve has caught on the plinth's corner. Arm returns pulling sleeve taut while the trolley tilts slightly, one wheel rising; black ball is clearly rolling back left toward student's foot. Student makes a small awkward sidestep. The connected causal tangle is funny; no flying debris, no injury. Caption: 'The correction adds another tug.'
PANEL 4: energy has mostly dissipated. Trolley resting skewed beside plinth, sleeve still draped, ball resting against student's black shoe. Student now sits on a low step looking thoughtfully at the contraption, hands relaxed, having stopped trying to force the demonstration. The original destination is still empty. Caption: 'We watch the attempt finish.'
Footer exact: 'The movement was calculated. The situation was not choreographed.'

Headline exact: 'A ROOM WITH OTHER PLANS'
Subtitle exact: 'ENDLESS MUSEUM · THE WORLD PLAYS OUT'
The museum courtyard contains a low powered turntable surrounded by THREE small nonhuman agent carts, each a plain squat white curved shell on four articulated black legs; no eyes, teeth or grotesque bodies. These are clearly designed local actors. One familiar black sphere is the attraction target. Shallow half-height movable partitions and a long soft elastic tether make routes change. Keep the same courtyard and cart designs across time. Each cart has a thin metal rim; collisions do not penetrate. The student starts an experiment and becomes an observer of its unintended outcome. Lighting develops from an ordered demonstration into a strange provisional assembly, no magical storm.
PANEL 1: student sets the black sphere onto center of the turntable. Three carts stand on separate approaches around it, each facing the sphere. Caption: 'Each body has a simple task.'
PANEL 2: two carts try to approach the sphere through a narrow gap beside a pale wheeled partition; their shells jam politely against each other, neither getting through. Third approaches from the back. Show visible contact and the student's surprised posture in background. Caption: 'Together, their tasks make a blockage.'
PANEL 3: the still-moving third cart pushes the side of that lightweight partition; the partition rolls aside, taking one end of a tether with it and turning the turntable a little. Former clear center now displaced; the black sphere rolls gently toward the edge but remains visible. The student reaches toward a control pedestal but has not pressed it. Caption: 'One obstruction rearranges the room.'
PANEL 4: wide calm aftermath: the movable partition now lies at a diagonal, two carts lean against each other at an odd angle, the third has reached the black sphere in a shallow corner created by the partition. No prescribed winner. Student sitting on museum step observes the unplanned grouping with a sketchbook closed beside them. Caption: 'I wait before naming what happened.'
Footer exact: 'An encounter has consequences before it has an explanation.'

Headline exact: 'THE BODY CARRIES ITS HISTORY'
Subtitle exact: 'ENDLESS MUSEUM · ATTACHMENT AND SPILLOVER'
One sculpture-body grows from the recurring shiny black sphere into an awkward, compelling assemblage of obsolete domestic and digital things: a salvaged pale-pink game controller shell, a mint corrugated tube, a lightweight translucent bag, two small white packaging cups and a simple polished metal hoop. Keep the distinctive same found parts from panel to panel. Their colors are muted, surfaces worn, no logos. NO body horror, no goo explosion, no sentimental perfection. The black sphere remains the identifiable original core. A low plinth, shallow floor depression and gentle ventilator make forces visible through material response.
PANEL 1: student holds the black sphere over a simple plinth. On the plinth the few found parts are neatly laid out, visibly chosen for potential use. Caption: 'Each attachment promised another use.'
PANEL 2: parts are now joined around the sphere by clearly visible small cords and hoop: tube curling to one side, bag tied above, controller shell hanging low. Student carefully lifts the asymmetrical assemblage; it tilts toward the hanging shell. Caption: 'Together, they change what the body can bear.'
PANEL 3: student has set the assemblage down on the plinth. A floor fan gently inflates the tied bag and pulls sideways. The hoop catches the plinth edge; the packaging cups tumble into the shallow depression. Show observable tension, collision and weight, NOT objects floating without cause. Student crouches at a distance, attentive, not instantly fixing it. Caption: 'The room joins in.'
PANEL 4: a quiet unexpected still life after motion settles: black sphere nestled partly in the hoop at the plinth edge, controller shell supported by floor, tube bent between them, bag slack, cups forming an accidental cradle. The student kneels and studies this bodily relation of objects without sorting it back into tidy components. The assembly looks ambiguous, touching, odd, materially grounded. Caption: 'It has become something we did not name.'
Footer exact: 'What looked like an accessory has become part of the conditions.'
